sentences.text: Inland lakes, rivers and many state waters use regulatory markers from the Uniform State Waterway Marking System.
An orange diamond warns of danger, such as a rock or shoal, with the hazard described in black letters.
A diamond with a cross inside means boats keep out, such as a swimming area or dam.
An orange circle marks a controlled area, such as a speed limit, idle speed or no-wake zone, very common in Florida’s manatee zones.
An orange square gives information, such as directions.
A white buoy with a blue horizontal band is a mooring buoy.
